extracted.intended_audience: Title IX coordinators, school administrators, higher-education legal counsel, and Title IX personnel
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements for school recipients to investigate, adjudicate, and respond to sexual harassment under Title IX, focusing on the presumption of non-responsibility, burden of proof, supportive measures, impartiality, and related protections. Intended to guide creation and evaluation of grievance processes and trainings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of non-responsibility (§106.45(b)(1)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must not treat the respondent as responsible until conclusion of the grievance process; the presumption is included in the initial written notice sent to both parties after a formal complaint has been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presumption is intended to ensure the recipient applies the chosen standard of evidence correctly and does not prejudge responsibility. It is not a statement about a respondent's credibility or truthfulness, does not shift the burden of proof to the complainant, and recipients must still objectively evaluate all relevant evidence. The presumption reinforces fair treatment and legitimacy of outcomes rather than protecting any particular group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof rests on the recipient
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations place the burden of proof solely on the recipient — not on a complainant or respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must gather relevant evidence and reach a determination regarding responsibility only if the evidence meets the recipient's selected standard of evidence. The presumption of non-responsibility complements this by preventing recipients from treating respondents as responsible before the recipient has met its burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures obligation (§106.44(a) and §106.30)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer complainants supportive measures designed to restore or preserve equal educational access, with or without a grievance process pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offering supportive measures is required promptly upon actual knowledge of sexual harassment. Supportive measures should not be conditioned on a complainant participating in a grievance process and must avoid unreasonably burdening the respondent. Medical-school-specific limitations do not negate the recipient's obligation to consider reasonable supportive measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on punishing respondent without a fair grievance process
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are prohibited from punishing a respondent without following a fair grievance process; recipients must apply the presumption of non-responsibility until the conclusion of the grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prohibition does not prevent emergency or interim actions where permitted (see emergency removal), but recipients cannot impose disciplinary sanctions absent the fair procedures required by §106.45. The presumption cannot be used as an excuse to ignore complainant needs or to avoid objectively evaluating evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on retaliation (§106.71(a)) and limits on sanctioning for false statements (§106.71(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations prohibit retaliation against any person exercising rights under Title IX. Charging an individual with a code-of-conduct violation for making a materially false statement in bad faith during a grievance process does not itself constitute retaliation if the recipient determines the statement was materially false and in bad faith and that determination is not based solely on the outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must be cautious before disciplining parties for alleged false statements; a determination that a party made a materially false statement requires evidence of bad faith and cannot rely only on the result of the grievance proceeding. This protects parties from being punished merely because the outcome did not favor them.

rubrics_metrics.name: No credibility determinations based on party status (§106.45(b)(1)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may not base credibility determinations on a person's status as a complainant or respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators and decision-makers must refrain from drawing inferences about credibility solely because someone is a complainant or respondent. The presumption of non-responsibility is distinct from any presumption about credibility and should not be interpreted as disbelieving complainants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality and required training for Title IX personnel (§106.45(b)(1)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: All Title IX personnel must serve impartially, without prejudging the facts at issue or bias toward complainants or respondents, and recipients must provide training to avoid bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients have discretion regarding training content and approaches provided they meet §106.45(b)(1)(iii) requirements. Training should address bias, ensure personnel do not prejudge responsibility, and support objective fact-finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal procedural participation rights for both parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural requirements of §106.45 equalize the rights of complainants and respondents to participate in investigation and adjudication by presenting each party's own view of the evidence and desired case outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equal procedural rights mean both parties have equivalent opportunities to present evidence and arguments, but do not imply equal allocation of the burden of proof — the burden remains with the recipient. These protections ensure complainants have meaningful opportunity to be heard equivalent to respondents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and application of standard of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must select and apply either the preponderance of the evidence standard or the clear and convincing evidence standard; the Title IX grievance process must not adopt the criminal 'beyond a reasonable doubt' standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presumption of non-responsibility helps ensure recipients correctly apply their selected standard of evidence. Recipients may not convert the proceeding into a criminal-style process by applying a higher standard than permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to respond to actual knowledge of sexual harassment (§106.44(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are required to respond promptly to actual knowledge of sexual harassment in their education program or activity, including by offering supportive measures to the complainant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to respond to actual knowledge can violate the regulations and jeopardize a recipient's federal funding. The presumption of non-responsibility does not permit ignoring complaints; recipients must objectively evaluate evidence and offer supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency or interim removal authority (§106.44(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.44(c) allows emergency removals of respondents prior to conclusion of a grievance process (or where no grievance process is pending) to protect community safety where an immediate threat exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emergency removals are distinct from disciplinary punishment and are permitted to protect safety. Recipients must still follow procedural safeguards appropriate to emergency actions and ensure they do not unreasonably burden respondents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on inferring 'false allegations' from non-responsibility findings
rubrics_metrics.description: A determination of non-responsibility is not equivalent to a finding that a complainant made a false allegation; allegations may be true but lack sufficient evidence, or may be inaccurate without intentional falsity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must avoid characterizing every non-responsibility finding as evidence of a false report. Discipline for false statements requires a separate finding of a materially false statement made in bad faith, not merely the outcome of the grievance process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability limited to Title IX sexual harassment grievance proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: These final regulations and the presumption of non-responsibility are focused on Title IX sexual harassment grievance processes and do not impose requirements on recipients' other student misconduct proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although features like presumption, burden allocation, and impartial procedures may be beneficial elsewhere, the regulation does not mandate extending these Title IX-specific rules to non-Title IX misconduct cases (e.g., cheating, theft). Recipients retain discretion over other disciplinary processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling allegations involving respondents outside recipient's disciplinary authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Where respondents are not enrolled or employed by the recipient (e.g., patients or visitors), recipients have discretion to dismiss a formal complaint or investigate and adjudicate and may implement remedies like no-trespass orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should evaluate each case independently; lack of disciplinary authority over a respondent does not excuse the recipient from responding to harassment that occurred in the recipient's program or activity and providing supportive measures for complainants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption's purpose: fairness, accuracy, and perceived legitimacy
rubrics_metrics.description: The presumption of non-responsibility is designed to improve the accuracy and legitimacy of outcomes in each individual formal complaint of sexual harassment and to prevent injustice to any complainant or respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory emphasis is on reliable determinations and perception of legitimacy. The presumption helps ensure recipients do not prejudge facts and that determinations are seen as fair, which supports confidence in remediation and disciplinary outcomes.
